definition_zh: 烧瓶；随身扁酒壶；保温瓶；火药壶；长颈细口瓶；一瓶之量
definition_en: a small bottle with a narrow neck, used in laboratories, in a pocket, or for keeping drinks hot
core_image: 一只细颈小瓶攥在手里，瓶壁微凉，瓶塞一拧就封住
scene: 实验室的架子上并排放着几只玻璃瓶，其中一只正冒着白汽。She swirled the blue liquid in the flask and set it on the tripod.
sceneCN: 这里 flask 是「实验室烧瓶」（第 1 个义项：化学实验用的玻璃容器）；句意：她摇匀烧瓶里的蓝色液体，把它放到三脚架上。

pos.zh: 名词：烧瓶；随身扁酒壶；保温瓶；火药壶；长颈瓶；一瓶之量

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ful 构成，义为「一瓶之量」
由本词加指小后缀 -et 构成，义为「小瓶」，现已少用
由本词与形容词化成分构成，义为「瓶状的」

senses.title: A glass vessel for laboratory work
senses.definition: a glass container with a rounded or conical body and a narrow neck, used in laboratories for heating, mixing, or holding liquids
senses.definitionCN: 瓶身圆或呈锥形、瓶颈细窄的玻璃容器，实验室里用来加热、混合或存放液体
senses.example: She swirled the blue liquid in the flask and set it on the tripod.
senses.exampleCN: 她摇匀烧瓶里的蓝色液体，把它放到三脚架上。
senses.why: The word is a bottle word first; glassblowers gave the bottle a narrow neck so a stopper would fit and a hand could hold it over a flame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先是「瓶子」：吹玻璃的人把瓶颈做细，好让瓶塞塞得紧，手也能在火焰上方握住它。

senses.title: A flat bottle for strong drink
senses.definition: a small flat bottle, often of metal or thick glass, carried in a pocket and filled with spirits
senses.definitionCN: 常为金属或厚玻璃制的小扁瓶，揣在口袋里，用来装烈酒
senses.example: He offered me a sip from the flask in his coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他从大衣口袋里掏出扁酒壶，让我喝了一口。
senses.why: A bottle made for a pocket must be flat and curved: the same vessel, reshaped so the drink can travel with its owner.
senses.whyCN: 为口袋而做的瓶子必须又扁又弯：还是同一只容器，只是改了形状，好让酒跟着主人走。

senses.title: A vacuum flask that holds temperature
senses.definition: a double-walled container with a vacuum between the walls, which keeps hot drinks hot and cold drinks cold for hours
senses.definitionCN: 双层壁之间抽成真空的容器，能让热饮保温、冷饮保冷数小时
senses.example: We filled the vacuum flask with tea before the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行前，我们把保温瓶灌满了茶。
senses.why: The bottle already holds liquid; adding a vacuum gap lets it hold heat as well, so the word gains a second job.
senses.whyCN: 瓶子本来只负责装液体；加一层真空夹层后，它连温度也一起装住，这个词于是多了一项工作。

senses.title: A small bottle for gunpowder
senses.definition: a small container of horn, leather, or metal, used to carry gunpowder for a muzzle-loading firearm
senses.definitionCN: 用兽角、皮革或金属做的小容器，为前装火器携带火药
senses.example: The hunter refilled his powder flask before the next shot.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人重新把火药壶装满，准备下一枪。
senses.why: Before paper cartridges, a shooter poured loose powder from a small bottle at his belt; that bottle was a flask.
senses.whyCN: 在纸壳弹药出现之前，射手要从腰带上的小瓶里倒出散装火药；那只小瓶就是 flask。

senses.title: A narrow-necked bottle for oil or water
senses.definition: a bottle with a long slender neck, often of pottery or glass, used for oil, perfume, or water on a journey
senses.definitionCN: 瓶颈细长的瓶子，多为陶制或玻璃制，旅途中用来装油、香水或水
senses.example: A cracked pilgrim flask lay beside the old well.
senses.exampleCN: 一只裂了缝的朝圣者水壶躺在旧井边。
senses.why: The slender neck slows the pour, so a little oil or water can be carried a long way without being lost.
senses.whyCN: 细长的瓶颈让倒出的速度变慢，一点油或水因此能被带很远而不至于洒掉。

senses.title: The amount one flask holds
senses.definition: the quantity of liquid that fills a single flask, as in a flask of whisky
senses.definitionCN: 装满一只瓶子的液体量，如 a flask of whisky（一瓶威士忌）这一说法
senses.example: They shared a flask of whisky on the cold drive home.
senses.exampleCN: 在寒冷的回家路上，他们分喝了一瓶威士忌。
senses.why: Any container word can stand for its contents; the flask, small and sealed, becomes the unit the drink is counted in.
senses.whyCN: 任何容器词都能代替它所装的东西；扁小密封的 flask 于是成了计量这种酒的单位。

intro.en: Flask is a bottle word of Germanic stock that reached English through Old French; the laboratory sense is a modern narrowing.
intro.cn: flask 是日耳曼语系的「瓶子」词，经古法语进入英语；实验室义是现代的收窄用法。

items.en: Flasca is recorded as a bottle or flask, probably borrowed from a Germanic word rather than inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 flasca 记作「瓶、壶」，一般认为借自日耳曼语，而非拉丁语本族词。

items.en: Flasca means bottle in Old High German; German Flasche and Dutch fles keep the same shape.
items.cn: 古高地德语 flasca 意为「瓶子」，德语 Flasche 与荷兰语 fles 保持同一形态。

items.en: Flasque carries the bottle word into French, together with the diminutive flacon.
items.cn: 古法语 flasque 把这个「瓶子」词带入法语，并衍生出指小的 flacon。

items.en: Flask is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, meaning a bottle for liquid.
items.cn: flask 在十四世纪的英语文献中出现，义为装液体的瓶子。

items.en: Powder flasks and pocket flasks give the word its military and personal senses.
items.cn: 火药壶与随身酒壶让这个词获得军事与私人的用法。

items.en: Laboratory glassware takes the name in the nineteenth century, and the vacuum flask follows in the 1890s.
items.cn: 十九世纪的实验室玻璃器皿沿用了这个名字；保温瓶则出现在十九世纪九十年代。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the bottle family; the near-meaning group gathers other containers that are not bottles in the same sense.
note.cn: 形近组收「瓶子」词族；近义组收其他容器词，它们与 flask 的「瓶」并不完全同义。

entries.definition: A small flask; the diminutive is now archaic but still recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小瓶」，由本词加指小后缀构成，现已古旧但仍有记录。

entries.definition: A small bottle for perfume, from the same Latin bottle word and its French diminutive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「香水小瓶」，与本词同出拉丁语「瓶」词，属法语指小形式。

entries.definition: The amount that one flask holds.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一瓶之量」，由本词加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A general container for liquids, usually of glass or plastic; broader and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瓶子」，是液体容器的通称，范围更宽、语气中立。

entries.definition: A vacuum container for drinks; a trade name used as a common noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保温瓶」，原为商标名，现作普通名词使用。

entries.definition: A water container carried by a soldier or a walker.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「军用水壶、旅行水壶」，专供士兵或步行者携带饮水。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real bottle root, the compound names the word appears in, and the shapes the vessel takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「瓶子」词根、这个词实际出现的复合名称，以及容器的各种形状。

normal.en: Flask and the German Flasche are cousins: both are bottle words from the same Germanic stock.
normal.cn: flask 与德语 Flasche 是表亲：两者都是同一日耳曼语源里的「瓶子」词。

normal.en: A hip flask is flat on purpose, so that it fits against a hip.
normal.cn: hip flask 故意做成扁的，好贴着髋部放进口袋。

normal.en: A vacuum flask keeps heat in because the gap between its walls holds almost no air.
normal.cn: vacuum flask 能保温，因为两层壁之间的空隙几乎没有空气。

normal.en: The Erlenmeyer flask is named after the chemist who gave it its cone shape.
normal.cn: Erlenmeyer flask 以设计出锥形瓶身的化学家命名。

normal.en: Nothing in the root says laboratory: a flask was any bottle before science narrowed the word.
normal.cn: 词根本身没有「实验室」的意思：在科学把它收窄之前，flask 就是普通的瓶子。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow-necked bottle on a tripod, blue liquid turning slowly at its bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只细颈瓶架在三脚架上，蓝色液体在瓶底慢慢旋转。

abstract.en: Feel the flat metal bottle against a coat pocket, warm from the body and heavy with drink.
abstract.cn: 想象扁金属壶贴在大衣口袋上，被体温焐热，沉甸甸地装着酒。

abstract.en: See steam curl inside the glass walls of a thermos, stopped by the empty gap behind them.
abstract.cn: 想象热气在保温瓶的玻璃壁内卷曲，被壁后的空隙挡住。

examples.en: The technician heated the flask over a small flame.
examples.cn: 技术员在小火焰上加热烧瓶。

examples.en: He kept a flask of brandy in his desk drawer.
examples.cn: 他在书桌抽屉里放着一瓶白兰地。

examples.en: Rows of flasks stood on the shelf, each with a paper label.
examples.cn: 架子上排着一列烧瓶，每只都贴着纸质标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗拉斯克」——听着像「伏了水」的壶：一只细颈扁瓶，随身的酒与水都装得下；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自晚期拉丁语 flasca「瓶、壶」，可能借自日耳曼语（同源词如古高地德语 flasca、德语 Flasche、荷兰语 fles）；更早来源不确定。经古法语 flasque 进入中古英语，十四世纪起指「装液体的瓶子」，十九世纪起指实验室玻璃器皿与保温瓶。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of flask all name the same vessel at different scales: a laboratory bottle, a pocket bottle, an insulated bottle, a powder bottle, an old narrow-necked bottle, and the amount such a bottle holds.
sensesIntro.cn: flask 的六个义项都是同一只容器在不同尺度上的名字：化学家的瓶子、口袋里的瓶子、保温的瓶子、装火药的瓶子、古代细颈瓶，以及这样一只瓶子所装的量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow-necked bottle small enough to hold in one hand and tight enough to keep what it carries.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只细颈小瓶，小到能一手握住，密封到能保住里面的东西。

branches.en: THE LAB: the bottle becomes glassware that can take a flame.
branches.cn: 实验室线：瓶子变成能受火焰加热的玻璃器皿。

branches.en: THE POCKET: a flat bottle travels with its owner, and measures the drink it holds.
branches.cn: 随身线：扁瓶跟着主人走，也成了它所装之酒的量。

branches.en: THE VACUUM: an empty gap between the walls lets the bottle hold heat too.
branches.cn: 真空线：双层壁之间的空隙让瓶子连温度也装住。

branches.en: THE POWDER: what once held liquid holds gunpowder for a muzzle-loader.
branches.cn: 火药线：原本装液体的容器改而替前装火器装火药。

branches.en: THE OLD ROAD: a long neck pours slowly, so oil and water survive a journey.
branches.cn: 古道线：细长的瓶颈倒得慢，油和水因此能熬过一段旅程。

intro.en: Flask is a Germanic bottle word with French and Latin neighbours; English builds its small family with ordinary suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: flask 是日耳曼语系的「瓶子」词，与法语、拉丁语相邻；英语用普通后缀与复合方式扩展出一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin flasca is the recorded bridge between the Germanic bottle word and Old French flasque; the deeper source is not settled.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 flasca 是日耳曼「瓶子」词与古法语 flasque 之间有记录的中转；更早的来源尚未定论。

items.example: Flasca is the form that bridges Germanic and French.
items.exampleCN: flasca 是连接日耳曼语与法语的形式。

items.example: Its stem flascon- gave the French diminutive flacon.
items.exampleCN: 它的词干 flascon- 给出法语指小形式 flacon。

items.example: Old French carried the word north to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把这个词向北带到了英语。

items.example: The diminutive marks a smaller bottle.
items.exampleCN: 指小形式标出更小的瓶子。

items.meaning: a bottle with a narrow neck
items.example: English keeps the noun from the fourteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语从十四世纪起沿用这个名词。

items.example: The suffix -et shrinks the bottle.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -et 把瓶子变小。

items.example: It forms flasket.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flasket。

items.example: It forms flaskful.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flaskful。

items.example: Flaskful counts the contents, not the bottle.
items.exampleCN: flaskful 计量的是内容物，不是瓶子。

items.example: The compound describes a bottle outline.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词描述瓶子的轮廓。

definition_zh: 奉承；讨好；使感到荣幸；使显得好看；使自鸣得意
definition_en: to praise someone insincerely in order to please or persuade them, or to make someone or something seem better than it is
core_image: 一只手把皱起的布面抹平：话说得顺，棱角就没了
scene: 面试前，他在走廊尽头对着玻璃反复练习微笑。He flattered the interviewer and then asked for a salary above the range.
sceneCN: 这里 flatter 是「奉承、讨好」（第 1 个义项：为讨好而说好话）；句意：他奉承了面试官，随后提出的薪水高于该职位的区间。

pos.zh: 动词：奉承；讨好；使感到荣幸；使显得好看；使自鸣得意

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -y 构成，义为「奉承话；恭维」
由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「奉承者；拍马的人」
由本词加 -ing 构成，作形容词义为「讨好的；显好看的」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「不讨好的；暴露缺点的」

senses.title: To praise someone insincerely
senses.definition: to praise someone more than they deserve, usually in order to win favour or get something
senses.definitionCN: 过分称赞某人，通常是为了赢得欢心或得到好处
senses.example: He flattered the manager shamelessly before asking for the day off.
senses.exampleCN: 他先是对经理大肆奉承，然后才提出请一天假。
senses.why: The word is tied to a flat root: praise that smooths a person down, taking the ridges out of a refusal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与表示「平」的词根有关：奉承就是把对方抹平，把拒绝的棱角磨掉。

senses.title: To make someone feel honoured
senses.definition: to please someone by showing that they are admired or valued, often in the phrase be flattered
senses.definitionCN: 通过表示钦佩或看重让对方高兴，常用于 be flattered 这一说法
senses.example: I was flattered by the invitation to speak at the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 受邀在会议上发言，让我感到荣幸。
senses.why: If praise can smooth a person, it can also warm them: being noticed feels like a gift, even when the words are not needed.
senses.whyCN: 既然称赞能把人抹平，它也能把人焐暖：被看见本身就像一份礼物，哪怕这些话并不必要。

senses.title: To make someone or something look better
senses.definition: to make a person, place, or thing appear more attractive or successful than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 使人、地方或事物显得比实际更好看或更成功
senses.example: That angle flatters the old house and hides the broken roof.
senses.exampleCN: 那个角度让这栋老房子显得好看，也遮住了破损的屋顶。
senses.why: The smoothing image turns visual: a flattering light or cut removes the shadow that would show the flaw.
senses.whyCN: 「抹平」的意象转到视觉上：讨好的光线或剪裁去掉了会暴露缺陷的阴影。

senses.title: To encourage a false good opinion of oneself
senses.titleCN: 使自鸣得意；使自我陶醉
senses.definition: to make someone believe they are better or more important than they are, especially in the phrase flatter oneself
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信自己比实际更好或更重要，尤用于 flatter oneself 这一说法
senses.example: He flattered himself that the project could not manage without him.
senses.exampleCN: 他自以为这个项目少了他就运转不了。
senses.why: Praise aimed at oneself becomes a mirror that smooths every fault, so the person sees a better copy.
senses.whyCN: 说给自己的好话成了一面抹平所有缺点的镜子，人于是在镜中看见一个更好的复制品。

senses.title: Flatter to deceive: promise more than it delivers
senses.definition: in the phrase flatter to deceive, to look promising or successful while in fact failing to deliver
senses.definitionCN: 用于 flatter to deceive 这一说法，指看起来有前途或很成功，实际却兑现不了
senses.example: The new system flattered to deceive for a year before the errors piled up.
senses.exampleCN: 新系统表面风光了一年，随后错误越积越多。
senses.why: Smooth words can cover a weak result: the promise looks polished, and that polish is exactly what misleads.
senses.whyCN: 顺耳的话能盖住糟糕的结果：承诺被打磨得发亮，而正是这层光亮让人误判。

intro.en: Flatter is a French verb of uncertain deeper origin; the flat root is a common suggestion, not a settled fact.
intro.cn: flatter 是一个法语来源的动词，更早的词源不确定；「平」的词根只是常见推测，并非定论。

items.en: The word appears in Old French, but its earlier source is uncertain; a common suggestion links it to a Germanic root meaning flat, to smooth.
items.cn: 这个词见于古法语，更早的来源不确定；常见说法把它与表示「平、抹平」的日耳曼语词根联系起来。

items.en: Flater means to flatter, to caress, and also to deceive, with all three shades present.
items.cn: 古法语 flater 同时有「奉承、抚弄、欺骗」三层意思。

items.en: Flatteren enters English in the fourteenth century as a verb of pleasing speech.
items.cn: flatteren 于十四世纪进入英语，指说讨人喜欢的话。

items.en: The sense widens to pleasing the eye: a portrait or a dress can flatter its subject.
items.cn: 词义扩展到视觉：画像或衣服也能美化其对象。

items.en: Reflexive and idiomatic uses appear: flatter oneself, and the phrase flatter to deceive.
items.cn: 反身与习语用法出现：flatter oneself 以及 flatter to deceive 这一说法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the flattery family; the near-meaning group holds words for saying good things, with different honesty and intensity.
note.cn: 形近组是「奉承」词族；近义组收「说好话」一类的词，它们的真诚程度与力度各不相同。

entries.definition: Insincere praise, or the words used to win favour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奉承话、恭维」，由本词加后缀 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A person who flatters others for advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奉承者」，由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Making someone look better or feel more important than is true.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「讨好的、显好看的」，由本词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: To say something nice to someone, usually sincerely and without a hidden aim.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「称赞、恭维」，通常是真心话，不带隐藏目的。

entries.definition: To express approval or admiration, openly and sincerely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「赞扬、表扬」，公开而真诚。

entries.definition: To behave servilely towards someone in order to win favour; more negative than flatter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「谄媚、讨好」，姿态更卑微，贬义比 flatter 更重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French verb, the family nouns, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的法语动词、同族名词，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Flattery is the noun and a flatterer is the person; the verb keeps the action.
normal.cn: flattery 是名词，flatterer 是那个人，动词 flatter 保留的是动作。

normal.en: A common account ties flatter to a flat root: praise that smooths the surface of the person praised.
normal.cn: 常见说法把 flatter 与表示「平」的词根联系起来：奉承就是把人表面抹平。

normal.en: Feel flattered is the phrase for the pleasant side of being noticed.
normal.cn: feel flattered 这一说法表达的是「被看见」的愉快一面。

normal.en: A flattering dress changes how the body reads, not the body itself.
normal.cn: a flattering dress 改变的是身体给人的观感，而不是身体本身。

normal.en: Flatter to deceive is the warning label on a promise that only looks good.
normal.cn: flatter to deceive 是给「只看着好」的承诺贴上的警示标签。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing over crumpled cloth, leaving it smooth behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抚过皱起的布，走过之后布面就平了。

abstract.en: Picture a warm remark landing on a face, and the face opening like a curtain.
abstract.cn: 想象一句暖话落到对方脸上，那张脸像帘子一样舒展开。

abstract.en: Picture someone turning sideways in front of a mirror until the fall of the cloth hides every corner.
abstract.cn: 想象有人在镜前侧过身，直到衣料垂下的线条把每一处棱角都遮住。

examples.en: She flattered her boss and got the transfer she wanted.
examples.cn: 她奉承了老板，拿到了想要的调岗。

examples.en: The team felt flattered by the attention from the national press.
examples.cn: 全国媒体的关注让团队感到荣幸。

examples.en: The low light in the restaurant is flattering to everyone at the table.
examples.cn: 餐厅里昏暗的灯光让桌边每个人都显得好看。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「服了他」——好话说得人服服帖帖，就是奉承；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自古法语 flater「奉承、抚弄、欺骗」，更早来源不确定；常见说法把它的源头与日耳曼语中表示「平」的词根联系起来，本义近于「抹平、抚平表面」，再引申为「说顺耳的话、使人心平」。中古英语作 flatteren。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from smoothing words to smoothing appearances: insincere praise, the pleasure of being noticed, a better-looking image, a flattered self, and a promise that only looks good.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从「抹平话语」走到「抹平外表」：虚假的称赞、被看见的喜悦、更好看的形象、被捧高的自我，以及只看着好的承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand smoothing the wrinkles out of a cloth until the surface lies flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把布上的褶子抹平，直到表面服帖。

branches.en: THE WORDS: praise is used as a tool to smooth the way to a favour.
branches.cn: 话语线：称赞被当作工具，用来抹平通往好处的路。

branches.en: THE FEELING: being noticed warms the person who is praised.
branches.cn: 感受线：被看见这件事把被称赞的人焐暖。

branches.en: THE EYE: light, angle, or cut makes the object look better than it is.
branches.cn: 视觉线：光线、角度或剪裁让对象显得比实际更好。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: praise turned inward hides every fault from its owner.
branches.cn: 镜子线：转向自己的称赞替主人把每个缺点都藏起来。

branches.en: THE WARNING: what is only polished can still fail when tested.
branches.cn: 警示线：只是被抛光过的东西，一受检验仍会失灵。

intro.en: Flatter comes from a French verb rather than a Latin root; English builds the family with -y, -er, -ing and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: flatter 来自一个法语动词，而不是拉丁词根；英语用 -y、-er、-ing 与否定前缀 un- 扩展出这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Flatter has no recorded Latin source; the trail begins in Old French and is often traced to a Germanic root meaning flat.
latinIntro.cn: flatter 没有可考的拉丁语来源；线索起于古法语，常被追溯到日耳曼语中表示「平」的词根。

items.example: The French verb is the first recorded link.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词是最早有记录的一环。

items.example: English took the verb together with its French ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语连同法语词尾一起收下了这个动词。

items.example: The modern verb drops the old ending.
items.exampleCN: 现代动词去掉了旧的词尾。

items.example: It forms flattery from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成 flattery。

items.example: Flattery names the words themselves.
items.exampleCN: flattery 指那些话本身。

items.example: It forms flatterer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flatterer。

items.example: The suffix marks the person, not the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出人，而不是动作。

items.meaning: pleasing or making someone look good
items.example: The participle works as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词在这里作形容词用。

items.example: It forms unflattering.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unflattering。

items.example: The prefix reverses the compliment.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把称赞翻转过来。

definition_zh: 瑕疵；裂缝；缺陷；漏洞；弱点
definition_en: a small crack or fault in a thing, or a weakness that makes a plan, argument, character, or document imperfect
core_image: 瓷器釉面上一道细如发丝的裂线，灯一照就现出来
scene: 鉴定师举起那只旧碗，对着灯光慢慢转动，影子忽然顿住。A thin flaw ran across the glaze, and the price fell by half.
sceneCN: 这里 flaw 是「瑕疵、裂缝」（第 1 个义项：器物表面的细小裂缝）；句意：一道细缝横过釉面，价格因此降了一半。

pos.zh: 名词：瑕疵；裂缝；缺陷；漏洞；弱点

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「有缺陷的；有瑕疵的」
由本词加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无瑕的；完美的」
由 flawless 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「无瑕地；完美地」
由 flawless 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「无瑕；完美」

senses.title: A thin crack in a hard surface
senses.definition: a narrow break or crack in the surface of a hard material such as glass, stone, or glaze
senses.definitionCN: 玻璃、石头或釉面等硬质材料表面上的细窄裂口
senses.example: A thin flaw ran across the glaze, and the price fell by half.
senses.exampleCN: 一道细缝横过釉面，价格因此降了一半。
senses.why: The oldest image is a piece of stone or glaze that has broken along a line: what was continuous now has a seam.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是一块石料或釉面沿一条线断开：本来连续的东西有了接缝。

senses.title: A defect that spoils beauty or value
senses.definition: a small fault in a jewel, fabric, or made object that spoils its beauty or lowers its value
senses.definitionCN: 宝石、织物或制成品上的小毛病，破坏美感或降低价值
senses.example: The diamond was clear except for one tiny flaw near the edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗钻石通体通透，只在边缘附近有一处小小的瑕疵。
senses.why: Once a break is seen, it is judged: a crack in a gem stops being a shape and becomes a fault that a buyer will pay less for.
senses.whyCN: 裂口一旦被看见就会被评判：宝石里的裂线不再是形状，而是让买家压价的毛病。

senses.title: A fault in a plan or argument
senses.definition: a mistake or weak point in a plan, argument, system, or method that makes it fail or lose force
senses.definitionCN: 计划、论证、制度或方法中的错误或薄弱之处，使其失效或失去说服力
senses.example: The plan had one fatal flaw: it assumed the weather would hold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划有一个致命漏洞：它假定天气会一直晴好。
senses.why: Reasoning is built like a wall: one bad joint and the whole structure carries less weight, so the flaw is the joint that gives way.
senses.whyCN: 推理像墙一样垒起来：一处接缝没砌好，整面墙承重就差，flaw 就是那处会松动的接缝。

senses.title: A weakness in character
senses.definition: a fault in the character of a person that repeatedly causes trouble or harm
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格里反复惹出麻烦或伤害的毛病
senses.example: Generosity was his strength and his one flaw at the same time.
senses.exampleCN: 慷慨既是他的长处，也是他唯一的弱点。
senses.why: A person is treated as a made thing: the same seam that shows under strain is called a flaw in the character.
senses.whyCN: 人被当作一件做出来的东西：受力时露出的同一道接缝，在性格上就叫 flaw。

senses.title: A fault that makes a document invalid
senses.titleCN: 法律瑕疵；使文件失效的毛病
senses.definition: a fault in a legal document or procedure that weakens it or makes it invalid
senses.definitionCN: 法律文件或程序中的毛病，使其效力受损或归于无效
senses.example: The contract was set aside because of a flaw in its signature clause.
senses.exampleCN: 由于签署条款存在瑕疵，这份合同被撤销。
senses.why: Law borrows the material image: a document with a flaw has a seam that will split when it is tested in court.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了器物意象：有 flaw 的文件带着一道接缝，一旦在法庭上受力就会裂开。

intro.en: Flaw is first recorded in the fourteenth century; its deeper origin is uncertain, with the most common view pointing to a Scandinavian word for a slab or flake.
intro.cn: flaw 最早记于十四世纪，更早的来源不确定；最常见的看法把它指向斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「石板、薄片」的词。

items.en: The word has no settled Latin or French source; a common view connects it with a Scandinavian word for a slab of stone.
items.cn: 这个词没有确定的拉丁语或法语来源；常见看法把它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「石板」的词联系起来。

items.en: Flaga means a slab or flake of stone; a flaw would be a piece split off a hard surface.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 flaga 指石板或石片；flaw 原是从坚硬表面崩下的一片。

items.en: Flaw names a flake, a fragment, and then a crack in a surface.
items.cn: 中古英语 flaw 指薄片、碎片，进而指表面的裂缝。

items.en: The sense widens from matter to judgement: a flaw in a character, a plan, or an argument.
items.cn: 词义从器物扩展到评判：性格、计划或论证里的缺陷。

items.en: Technical and legal uses settle in: a flaw in a diamond, and a fatal flaw in a contract.
items.cn: 技术与法律用法固定下来：钻石的内含瑕疵，以及合同里的致命瑕疵。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on flaw itself; the near-meaning group holds other words for faults, each with a different field of use.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 flaw 本身构词；近义组收其他表示「毛病」的词，各自的使用范围不同。

entries.definition: Having a fault or defect; formed from flaw plus -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有缺陷的、有瑕疵的」，由本词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Without any fault; formed from flaw plus the negative suffix -less.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无瑕的、完美的」，由本词加否定后缀 -less 构成。

entries.definition: In a manner without any fault; the adverb of flawless.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无瑕地、完美地」，是 flawless 的副词形式。

entries.definition: A fault in a product or a system; more technical and neutral than flaw.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺陷、毛病」，多用于产品或系统，比 flaw 更技术化、更中立。

entries.definition: A mark that spoils the appearance of a surface, especially skin or paint.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瑕疵、污点」，专指破坏表面外观的痕迹，多用于皮肤或漆面。

entries.definition: A point where a person or system is easily hurt or defeated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「弱点、薄弱环节」，指人或者系统容易受损、被攻破之处。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Scandinavian origin, the -less family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的斯堪的纳维亚语源、带 -less 的词族，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Flaw and flawless sit in one family: the suffix -less removes exactly what the noun names.
normal.cn: flaw 与 flawless 同属一个词族：后缀 -less 去掉的正是这个名词所指的东西。

normal.en: A fatal flaw is the single defect that decides the outcome.
normal.cn: a fatal flaw 就是决定最终结果的那一处缺陷。

normal.en: Engineers say design flaw when the mistake is in the drawing, not in the part.
normal.cn: 当错误出在图纸而不是零件上时，工程师会说 design flaw。

normal.en: Flawed work can still work; trouble starts when the flaw carries the load.
normal.cn: 有瑕疵的东西也还能用；麻烦始于那处瑕疵正好要承重。

normal.en: A character flaw is a seam you carry, not one you can polish away.
normal.cn: character flaw 是随身带着的一道接缝，不是抛光就能磨掉的。

abstract.en: Picture a porcelain bowl turned under a lamp until a hairline crack lights up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只瓷碗在灯下慢慢转动，直到一道细如发丝的裂线忽然亮起。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass over a gem, where a tiny bubble sits deep inside the stone.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜照着一颗宝石，里面深处藏着一颗小气泡。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge drawing with one support line missing, so the model bends under the first weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桥梁图纸少画了一条支撑线，模型在第一次承重时就弯了。

examples.en: The vase was cheap because of a flaw in the rim.
examples.cn: 这只花瓶便宜，是因为瓶口有一处瑕疵。

examples.en: Critics found several flaws in the study.
examples.cn: 批评者在这项研究里发现了几处漏洞。

examples.en: A flaw in the software let the same order be charged twice.
examples.cn: 软件里的一处缺陷让同一笔订单被扣了两次款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「浮漏」——釉面上浮出一道会漏的细线，就是瑕疵；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为与古诺尔斯语 flaga「石板、薄片」有关，原指从坚硬表面崩下的一片；中古英语 flaw 于十四世纪记作「薄片、碎片、裂缝」，更早来源不确定。十六世纪起，词义从器物的裂缝扩展到性格、计划、论证与法律文件上的缺陷。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow one seam outward: a crack in a surface, a defect that lowers value, a fault in reasoning, a weakness in character, and a fault that voids a document.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项沿同一道接缝向外走：表面的裂缝、降低价值的瑕疵、推理中的漏洞、性格上的弱点，以及使文件失效的毛病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hairline crack across glazed porcelain, visible only when the light is right.
core.cn: 核心意象：釉面上细如发丝的一道裂线，只在光线合适时才看得见。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: a hard surface splits along a thin line.
branches.cn: 材料线：坚硬表面沿一条细线裂开。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the crack is judged, and beauty or value drops.
branches.cn: 器物线：裂口被评判，美感或价值随之下降。

branches.en: THE REASON: a weak joint in an argument gives way under weight.
branches.cn: 推理线：论证里一处薄弱的接缝在承重时松动。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same seam becomes a weakness of character.
branches.cn: 人物线：同一道接缝变成性格上的弱点。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: in law the seam splits and the paper loses its force.
branches.cn: 文件线：在法律上这道接缝裂开，文书随之失去效力。

intro.en: Flaw comes from Scandinavian stock, and English forms its family with -ed, -less, -ly and -ness rather than Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: flaw 来自斯堪的纳维亚语源，英语用 -ed、-less、-ly 与 -ness 构词，而不是拉丁语前缀。

latinIntro.en: Flaw has no Latin source at all: the trail runs from Old Norse flaga through Middle English, so no Latin entries are recorded here.
latinIntro.cn: flaw 完全没有拉丁语来源：线索从古诺尔斯语 flaga 经中古英语而来，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The Scandinavian noun supplies the earliest image.
items.exampleCN: 这个斯堪的纳维亚语名词提供最早的意象。

items.example: The noun narrows from a flake to a crack.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「薄片」收窄为「裂缝」。

items.example: The suffix -ed turns the noun into a description.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 把名词变成描述。

items.example: It forms flawed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flawed。

items.example: The negative suffix removes the fault.
items.exampleCN: 否定后缀把毛病去掉。

items.example: It forms flawless.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flawless。

items.example: The adverb marks how something is done.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词标出做事的完美程度。

items.example: It forms flawlessly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flawlessly。

items.meaning: the state of being without fault
items.example: The noun suffix names the state.
items.exampleCN: 名词后缀标出这种状态。

items.example: It forms flawlessness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flawlessness。

definition_zh: 跳蚤；跳蚤侵扰；跳蚤市场；带刺的斥责；跳蚤马戏团
definition_en: a very small wingless insect that jumps and feeds on the blood of animals, or the trouble it causes
core_image: 一只黑褐色小虫后腿一蹬，整只弹出去，落下时只剩一点痒
scene: 旧仓库的角落里堆着发霉的毯子，工人刚把最上面一条掀起来。A flea jumped from the blanket onto his sleeve.
sceneCN: 这里 flea 是「跳蚤」（第 1 个义项：会跳的吸血小虫）；句意：一只跳蚤从毯子跳到了他的袖子上。

pos.zh: 名词：跳蚤；跳蚤侵扰；跳蚤市场；带刺的斥责；跳蚤马戏团

derivatives.zh: 由 flea 与 bag 复合而成，义为「满是跳蚤的地方」，也指破旧的旅馆
由 flea 与 bane 复合而成，义为「飞蓬」，一种据传能驱蚤的植物
由 flea 与 bitten 复合而成，义为「被跳蚤咬的；破旧的」
由 flea 与 ridden 复合而成，义为「满是跳蚤的」

senses.title: The jumping blood-sucking insect
senses.definition: a very small wingless insect with strong hind legs that jumps and feeds on the blood of mammals and birds
senses.definitionCN: 一种极小的无翅昆虫，后腿强壮，会跳，靠吸食哺乳动物与鸟类的血为生
senses.example: A flea jumped from the blanket onto his sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 一只跳蚤从毯子跳到了他的袖子上。
senses.why: The old English name is simply the insect name; its whole image is the leap from one host to the next.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里的这个名字就是这种昆虫的名称；它的整个意象就是从一只宿主跳到另一只宿主。

senses.title: A plague of fleas on a place or animal
senses.definition: the condition of a place, animal, or person being covered with fleas
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、动物或人身上爬满跳蚤的状态
senses.example: The stray dog was thin and crawling with fleas.
senses.exampleCN: 那只流浪狗瘦得厉害，身上爬满了跳蚤。
senses.why: The plural turns the insect into a mass: not one flea but a condition that a host must be rid of.
senses.whyCN: 复数把这只昆虫变成一团：不是一只跳蚤，而是一种宿主必须摆脱的状态。

senses.title: Flea market: a market for old goods
senses.definition: in the phrase flea market, a market where cheap or second-hand goods are sold
senses.definitionCN: 用于 flea market 这一说法，指出售廉价货或旧货的市场
senses.example: They found the old lamp at a flea market on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们星期天在跳蚤市场找到了那盏旧灯。
senses.why: The French name of such a market means market of fleas; the flea marks goods so old and cheap that they might carry the insect.
senses.whyCN: 这类市场的法语名称意为「跳蚤的市场」；跳蚤标出货物又旧又便宜，旧到可能带着虫。

senses.title: A flea in the ear: a sharp rebuke
senses.definition: in the phrase a flea in the ear, a sharp warning or scolding that leaves someone stinging
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a flea in the ear 这一说法，指让人事后仍觉刺痛的一顿严厉警告或斥责
senses.example: He came back with a flea in the ear after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开完会，他挨了一顿严厉的斥责回来。
senses.why: The image is literal discomfort: a small biting insect inside the ear, so the words keep stinging after they are heard.
senses.whyCN: 意象是字面的不适：一只会咬的小虫钻进耳朵里，所以那些话听过之后还在刺痛。

senses.title: Flea circus: a show of performing fleas
senses.definition: in the phrase flea circus, a sideshow in which fleas are made to pull tiny carts or perform tricks
senses.definitionCN: 用于 flea circus 这一说法，指让跳蚤拉小车或表演动作的余兴节目
senses.example: The flea circus drew a crowd at the old fair.
senses.exampleCN: 跳蚤马戏团在旧时的集市上引来一群人围观。
senses.why: Once the insect could be handled, it became a performer: the smallest animal turned into the cheapest spectacle.
senses.whyCN: 这种昆虫一旦能被摆弄，就成了演员：最小的动物变成了最便宜的奇观。

intro.en: Flea is a native Germanic insect name; the English word descends from Old English, and the compounds are late additions.
intro.cn: flea 是日耳曼语本族的昆虫名称；英语这个词承自古英语，而那些复合词是后来才出现的。

items.en: The deeper Indo-European source is uncertain; the insect name is often linked to a root for fleeing or flying, but no single form is agreed.
items.cn: 更早的印欧语来源不确定；这种昆虫的名字常被认为与表示「逃、飞」的词根有关，但没有公认的单一形式。

items.en: Flauhaz is the reconstructed Germanic word for the flea, recovered from its descendants rather than from any text.
items.cn: flauhaz 是重构的日耳曼语「跳蚤」词，靠后代语言重建，而不是见于文本。

items.en: Fleah names the flea; the form is attested in glosses and word lists.
items.cn: 古英语 flēah 指跳蚤，见于注释与词表。

items.en: Fle and flea settle the modern spelling, and compounds begin to appear.
items.cn: 中古英语的写法定下现代拼写，复合词也开始出现。

items.en: Flea market and flea circus enter English in the nineteenth century, both borrowed from French usage.
items.cn: 跳蚤市场与跳蚤马戏团于十九世纪进入英语，两者都借自法语说法。

items.en: Flea collar and flea treatment become household words for pet care.
items.cn: 除蚤项圈与除蚤处理成为宠物护理的家常用语。

note.en: The look-alike group is the flea family of compounds and derivatives; the near-meaning group holds other small biting pests.
note.cn: 形近组是 flea 的复合词与派生词词族；近义组收其他小型叮咬害虫。

entries.definition: A place or bed full of fleas, and by extension a cheap dirty hotel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「满是跳蚤的地方」，引申指廉价肮脏的旅馆，由 flea 与 bag 复合而成。

entries.definition: A plant once believed to drive fleas away; the second element means bane or killer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飞蓬」，一种旧时被认为能驱蚤的植物，后半部分意为「祸害、杀灭者」。

entries.definition: Bitten by fleas, and by extension worn out or shabby.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被跳蚤咬的」，引申指「破旧的」，由 flea 与 bitten 复合而成。

entries.definition: A small eight-legged parasite that attaches to skin and sucks blood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜱」，一种八条腿的小寄生虫，附着在皮肤上吸血。

entries.definition: A small wingless insect that lives on hair or feathers and bites.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「虱子」，一种无翅小昆虫，生活在毛发或羽毛间并叮咬。

entries.definition: A very small arachnid that lives in dust, on plants, or on animals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「螨」，一种极小的蛛形动物，生活在灰尘、植物或动物身上。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Germanic insect name, its compounds, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的日耳曼语昆虫名称、它的复合词，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Flea belongs with German Floh and Dutch vlo: one Germanic insect under three names.
normal.cn: flea 与德语 Floh、荷兰语 vlo 同源：同一种日耳曼语昆虫有三个名字。

normal.en: The hind legs are made for jumping, so the flea is gone before a hand arrives.
normal.cn: 后腿天生用来跳，所以手还没到，跳蚤已经走了。

normal.en: Fleas on a pet are an infestation, not a single visitor.
normal.cn: 宠物身上的跳蚤是一种侵扰，而不是一位来访者。

normal.en: Flea market is a calque of the French market of fleas: the goods are old enough to carry the insect.
normal.cn: flea market 是法语「跳蚤的市场」的仿译：货物旧到可能带着这种虫。

normal.en: A flea collar is a band that keeps the insects off the animal.
normal.cn: 除蚤项圈是一条把这种虫挡在动物体外的带子。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket shaken once, and a dark speck springing off it and landing again.
abstract.cn: 想象毯子被抖了一下，一个黑褐色小点弹起，又落回原处。

abstract.en: Picture a thin dog scratching behind its ear, the fur full of tiny black specks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只瘦狗不停挠耳后，毛里全是细小的黑点。

abstract.en: Picture a folding table at a street corner, chipped bowls laid out with prices on card.
abstract.cn: 想象街角一张折叠桌，缺角的碗摆开来，价格写在纸板上。

examples.en: The cat scratched all night because of a flea.
examples.cn: 因为一只跳蚤，那只猫挠了一整夜。

examples.en: Fleas can jump many times their own body length.
examples.cn: 跳蚤能跳出自身身长的许多倍。

examples.en: She bought a chipped teapot at the flea market.
examples.cn: 她在跳蚤市场买了一只缺口茶壶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「飞离」——后腿一蹬就飞离原地，正是跳蚤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 flēah（也作 flēa）「跳蚤」，来自重构的原始日耳曼语 *flauhaz；同源词有古高地德语 flōh、德语 Floh、荷兰语 vlo。更早的印欧语来源不确定，一般认为与表示「逃、飞」的词根有关，但没有定论。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses start with the insect and then follow it into language: an infestation, a cheap market, a stinging rebuke, and a tiny circus.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从昆虫本身出发，再跟着它进入语言：跳蚤侵扰、旧货市场、带刺的斥责，以及一场微型马戏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark speck that springs off a blanket and lands on a sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个黑褐色的小点从毯子上弹起，落在袖子上。

branches.en: THE INSECT: a wingless body built around two jumping legs.
branches.cn: 昆虫线：一副无翅的身体，全靠两条会跳的腿。

branches.en: THE HOST: many fleas become a condition of the animal or the room.
branches.cn: 宿主线：许多跳蚤合起来，成了动物或房间的一种状态。

branches.en: THE MARKET: old cheap goods are named after the insect they might carry.
branches.cn: 市场线：又旧又便宜的货物，用它可能带着的虫子来命名。

branches.en: THE EAR: a bite inside the ear becomes words that keep stinging.
branches.cn: 耳朵线：钻进耳朵的一咬，变成事后仍在刺痛的话。

branches.en: THE SHOW: the smallest animal is trained into a spectacle.
branches.cn: 表演线：最小的动物被训练成一场奇观。

intro.en: Flea is a native Germanic word; English extends it mainly through compounds rather than suffixes, and the family is full of everyday pests and places.
intro.cn: flea 是日耳曼语本族词；英语主要靠复合而不是后缀来扩展它，这个词族里多是日常的害虫与场所。

latinIntro.en: Flea has no Latin source: the English word descends from Old English and a reconstructed Germanic form, while Latin used the unrelated pulex for the insect.
latinIntro.cn: flea 没有拉丁语来源：英语这个词承自古英语与重构的日耳曼语形式，拉丁语另用无关的 pulex 表示跳蚤。

items.example: The Old English form is the earliest written link.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语形式是最早有书面记录的一环。

items.example: Middle English shortens the long vowel in writing.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语在书写上把长元音缩短了。

items.example: The modern noun keeps the insect sense only.
items.exampleCN: 现代名词只保留昆虫义。

items.meaning: a market for cheap old goods
items.example: The compound borrows a French market name.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词借用了法语的市场名称。

items.example: The compound names a product for pets.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词给一种宠物用品命名。

items.example: The compound names an old sideshow.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词给一种旧时余兴节目命名。

items.example: It forms flea-bitten.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flea-bitten。

items.example: The adjective describes a shabby animal or place.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述破旧的动物或地方。

items.example: It forms flea-ridden.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 flea-ridden。

items.example: The adjective intensifies the infestation.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词强化了侵扰的程度。

items.example: The compound shifts from the animal to the place.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词从动物转到地方。

definition_zh: 闪烁；忽明忽暗；一闪；轻微颤动
definition_en: to shine or move with an unsteady, wavering light or motion
core_image: 黑暗中一支烛火忽明忽暗，随时可能熄灭
scene: 停电后的客厅只剩一支蜡烛，火苗在风里晃个不停。The candle flame began to flicker as the window opened.
sceneCN: 这里「flicker」是「闪烁、忽明忽暗」（第 2 个义项：光源本身明暗不定）；句意：窗户一开，烛火就开始摇曳闪烁。

pos.zh: 闪烁；忽明忽暗；轻快颤动

derivatives.zh: 由 flicker 加 -ing 构成，作形容词指「闪烁的；摇曳不定的」
flicker 与 -free 构成的复合形容词，义为「无闪烁的」

senses.title: Light that wavers
senses.definition: a light that shines unsteadily, growing brighter and dimmer
senses.definitionCN: 明暗不定、忽强忽弱的光
senses.example: A faint flicker came from the candle on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上蜡烛透出一点忽明忽暗的光。
senses.why: The core image is a flame that cannot hold a steady brightness, so the noun names that wavering light.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一簇无法稳定燃烧的火苗，名词便直接指这种明暗不定的光。

senses.title: To shine unsteadily
senses.definition: to shine with a light that keeps changing in brightness
senses.definitionCN: 亮度和明暗不断变化地发光
senses.example: The old lamp flickered and then went dark.
senses.exampleCN: 旧台灯闪了几下，然后熄灭了。
senses.why: The light source itself performs the wavering: the flame or bulb is the active subject of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 发光体自己做出忽明忽暗的动作，火苗或灯泡成为动词的主语，义项由此从名词转为动词。

senses.title: A brief feeling
senses.definition: a very short, faint appearance of a feeling or expression
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪或表情极短暂、极微弱地出现
senses.example: A flicker of doubt crossed her face.
senses.exampleCN: 她脸上掠过一丝疑虑。
senses.why: A feeling that appears and disappears like a weak flame borrows the same image: brief, faint, and unsteady.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像弱火一样刚亮起就暗下去，借用了同一幅画面：短暂、微弱、不稳定，于是从光延伸到内心。

senses.title: A small trembling movement
senses.definition: a quick, light, trembling movement of a body part
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部分快速而轻微的颤动
senses.example: The bird gave a flicker of its wings before it flew.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟起飞前轻轻抖了一下翅膀。
senses.why: The oldest physical sense is the fluttering of wings, a rapid back and forth motion that resembles a wavering flame.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理义是翅膀的扑动，这种快速来回的动作与摇曳的火光相似，因此同一词也能指轻微颤动。

senses.title: To move quickly across
senses.definition: to move with quick, light, wavering motion across a surface
senses.definitionCN: 以轻快、摇曳的动势掠过某个表面
senses.example: Shadows flickered across the wall as the fire burned.
senses.exampleCN: 火燃烧时，影子在墙上晃动掠过。
senses.why: When light and shadow move rapidly over a surface, the whole scene seems to flicker, so the verb extends from light to motion.
senses.whyCN: 光影在表面快速移动时，整个场景都像在闪动，动词便从光的闪烁延伸到一般的快速掠过。

intro.en: Flicker is probably echoic, and its closest relatives are Germanic words for fluttering and wavering.
intro.cn: flicker 很可能是拟声词，最亲近的同族词是日耳曼语中表示「扑动、摇曳」的词。

items.en: Flikeren names a fluttering or flapping motion in Middle English.
items.cn: 中古英语 flikeren 指扑动、拍翅的动作。

items.en: Flickeren is a close Germanic cousin meaning to flutter or waver.
items.cn: 中古低地德语 flickeren 是近亲，意为扑动、摇曳。

items.en: In the sixteenth century flicker records the verb sense of fluttering and quivering.
items.cn: 十六世纪 flicker 记下了「扑动、颤动」的动词义。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb also means to shine intermittently.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词又表示「断断续续地发光」。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the light sense and the small-movement sense in one word.
items.cn: 现代英语让「光」与「小动作」两个义项并存于同一个词。

note.en: Flicker is a wavering-light word, close to glimmer and shimmer and to the look-alike verb flick.
note.cn: flicker 是表示「光在摇动」的词，与 glimmer、shimmer 近义，也与形似的动词 flick 相邻。

entries.definition: to move or hit something with a quick light movement
entries.definitionCN: 轻弹；轻拂（与 flicker 拼写相近，来源可能相关但不确定）

entries.definition: shining with an unsteady light
entries.definitionCN: 闪烁的；摇曳的

entries.definition: to move quickly and lightly from place to place
entries.definitionCN: 轻快地移动（与 flicker 只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a faint, unsteady light
entries.definitionCN: 微光；隐约的闪光

entries.definition: to shine with a soft, trembling light
entries.definitionCN: 微微闪光；荡漾

entries.definition: to shine with small bright points of light
entries.definitionCN: 闪耀；闪光

normalIntro.en: Flicker belongs to a Germanic sound group that echoes flapping and trembling.
normalIntro.cn: flicker 属于一组模仿拍动与颤动的日耳曼语音，读音本身就带着晃动感。

normal.en: Say the word quickly and the two k sounds imitate a light flapping.
normal.cn: 快速念这个词，两个 k 音就像在模仿轻轻的拍动。

normal.en: A flicker of light is a light that cannot hold steady.
normal.cn: 「a flicker of light」就是无法稳定燃烧的光。

normal.en: A flicker of hope appears for a moment and then fades.
normal.cn: 「a flicker of hope」指一闪而过、随即淡去的希望。

normal.en: The form flickering describes a light or shadow that keeps moving.
normal.cn: flickering 描述不断晃动的光或影子。

normal.en: Compare flick, one quick movement, with flicker, a repeated wavering.
normal.cn: 对比 flick（一次轻快的动作）与 flicker（反复的摇曳）。

abstract.en: Picture a candle about to die in a draft.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛在穿堂风里将熄未熄。

abstract.en: See a bulb stutter twice before the room goes dark.
abstract.cn: 想象灯泡闪了两下，房间才彻底黑下来。

abstract.en: Watch doubt pass over a face like a weak light.
abstract.cn: 想象一丝疑虑像弱光一样掠过脸庞。

examples.en: The screen flickered and then went black.
examples.cn: 屏幕闪了几下，然后黑了。

examples.en: There was a flicker of hope in her voice.
examples.cn: 她的声音里有一丝希望。

examples.en: Shadows flickered across the cave wall.
examples.cn: 影子在洞壁上晃动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗利克」——火光快速一闪又暗下去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: flicker 一般认为来自中古英语 flikeren（拍翅、扑动），与中古低地德语 flickeren 同族，可能是拟声词；核心义「轻而快地来回晃动」，由拍翅扩展到火光忽明忽暗。

sensesIntro.en: Flicker starts from a light that cannot stay steady, then extends to fleeting feelings and to quick trembling motion.
sensesIntro.cn: flicker 从无法稳定燃烧的光出发，再延伸到一闪而过的情绪和轻快的颤动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a candle flame that brightens and dims in a draft.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支在风里忽明忽暗的烛火。

branches.en: The wavering light itself is the most literal sense.
branches.cn: 摇曳的光本身是最字面的义项。

branches.en: The verb names the action performed by that light.
branches.cn: 动词义指那束光自己做出的动作。

branches.en: A feeling can glow and fade like a weak flame.
branches.cn: 情绪可以像弱火一样亮起又暗下。

branches.en: The old wing-flapping sense survives as a small trembling movement.
branches.cn: 古老的拍翅义保留为轻微的颤动。

branches.en: Light and shadow moving across a surface extend to rapid motion.
branches.cn: 光影掠过表面，进一步引申为快速的移动。

intro.en: Flicker is a Germanic-looking verb with English forms in -s, -ed, and -ing, plus the compound flicker-free.
intro.cn: flicker 是一个日耳曼语系的动词，英语中带 -s、-ed、-ing 等词形，并有复合词 flicker-free。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded, so the word is treated as echoic or Germanic and no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语同源词，因此把该词视为拟声或日耳曼语来源，不列出拉丁词条。

items.example: The lamp flickers when the wind blows.
items.exampleCN: 起风时台灯会闪烁。

items.example: A flicker of light came from the hut.
items.exampleCN: 小屋里透出一点闪烁的光。

items.meaningCN: 动词第三人称单数形式
items.example: The candle flickers in the draft.
items.exampleCN: 蜡烛在穿堂风里闪烁。

items.example: The bulb flickered twice.
items.exampleCN: 灯泡闪了两下。

items.example: A flickering lamp lit the stairs.
items.exampleCN: 一盏闪烁的灯照着楼梯。

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词与动名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms flickering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 flickering。

items.meaning: to move or hit quickly and lightly
items.example: He flicked the switch with one finger.
items.exampleCN: 他用一根手指轻弹开关。

items.example: The suffix -free forms flicker-free.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -free 构成 flicker-free。

items.example: A flicker-free screen is easier on the eyes.
items.exampleCN: 无闪烁的屏幕对眼睛更友好。

definition_zh: 轻薄的；脆弱的；站不住脚的；不可信的
definition_en: thin and easily damaged, or weak and hard to believe
core_image: 一张一撕就破的薄纸，撑不住任何重量
scene: 搬家时才发现，纸箱薄得一提就变形。The flimsy cardboard box split before she reached the door.
sceneCN: 这里「flimsy」是「轻薄易破」（第 1 个义项：材料太薄而不结实）；句意：她还没走到门口，单薄的纸箱就裂开了。

pos.zh: 轻薄的；单薄的；脆弱的；站不住脚的

derivatives.zh: 由 flimsy 加 -ly 构成，指「单薄地；站不住脚地」
由 flimsy 加 -ness 构成，指「单薄；脆弱；缺乏说服力」

senses.title: Thin and easily broken
senses.definition: made of thin material that breaks or bends easily
senses.definitionCN: 由很薄的材料制成，容易破裂或弯折
senses.example: The flimsy box collapsed under the weight of the books.
senses.exampleCN: 那个单薄的箱子在书的重压下垮掉了。
senses.why: The core image is a sheet so thin that it tears at a touch, so the first sense is simply physical thinness.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一张薄到一碰就破的纸，因此第一个义项就是最直接的「物理上很薄」。

senses.title: Weakly built
senses.definition: not strongly built, so it shakes or falls apart easily
senses.definitionCN: 建造得不牢固，容易摇晃或散架
senses.example: They sheltered in a flimsy hut made of sticks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们躲进一间用树枝搭成的脆弱小屋。
senses.why: Thin material cannot make a solid frame, so poor construction grows out of the same thinness.
senses.whyCN: 薄材料撑不起坚固的骨架，因此「建造不牢」这个义项从同一种「薄」自然生长出来。

senses.title: Hard to believe
senses.definition: weak and unconvincing as an explanation or excuse
senses.definitionCN: 作为解释或借口显得薄弱、不能让人相信
senses.example: His flimsy excuse convinced nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 他那站不住脚的借口没能说服任何人。
senses.why: An excuse as thin as paper tears at the first question, so physical thinness becomes weakness in reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 借口像纸一样薄，遇到第一个追问就被撕破，于是「薄」转化为「道理站不住」。

senses.title: Lacking solid support
senses.definition: resting on evidence or reasoning too weak to support it
senses.definitionCN: 所依据的证据或推理太弱，撑不起结论
senses.example: The argument rests on flimsy evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论点建立在不可靠的证据上。
senses.why: When the material under a claim is thin, the claim cannot stand, which is the evidential version of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 支撑结论的材料太薄，结论就立不住；这正是同一意象在「证据」层面的说法。

senses.title: Light and insubstantial
senses.definition: light and thin in a way that feels insubstantial
senses.definitionCN: 又轻又薄，给人不实在的感觉
senses.example: A flimsy curtain moved in the least breeze.
senses.exampleCN: 一片轻薄的窗帘被最轻微的风吹动了。
senses.why: The feel of thin cloth in the air keeps the literal sense of lightness without adding the idea of breaking.
senses.whyCN: 薄布在空气中的触感保留了「轻」的字面义，但不强调「破」，于是分化出「轻薄飘忽」这一支。

intro.en: Flimsy appears in English in the eighteenth century, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: flimsy 在十八世纪进入英语，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: No single source is agreed for flimsy, and dictionaries treat it as unexplained.
items.cn: flimsy 的来源没有公认结论，词典一般把它标为来源不明。

items.en: Flim-flam, meaning nonsense or trickery, is recorded in the sixteenth century and may be a relative.
items.cn: 十六世纪记有 flim-flam（胡扯、欺骗），它可能是 flimsy 的近亲。

items.en: Flimsy first describes thin cloth and paper that tear easily.
items.cn: flimsy 最初描述容易撕破的薄布和薄纸。

items.en: The word extends to weak structures and to excuses that will not stand.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到脆弱的结构，以及站不住脚的借口。

items.en: Today flimsy covers both physical thinness and a lack of solid proof.
items.cn: 今天 flimsy 同时覆盖物理上的薄和证据上的不牢靠。

note.en: Flimsy is a thinness word, close to fragile and frail, and possibly related to the older flim-flam.
note.cn: flimsy 是表示「薄」的词，与 fragile、frail 近义，并可能与更早的 flim-flam 有关。

entries.definition: a thin layer or sheet of material
entries.definitionCN: 薄膜；胶片（与 flimsy 只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: nonsense or trickery
entries.definitionCN: 胡扯；欺骗（与 flimsy 来源可能相关，但无定论）

entries.definition: in a weak or thin way
entries.definitionCN: 单薄地；站不住脚地

entries.definition: easily broken or damaged
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的；脆弱的

entries.definition: weak and easily harmed
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱的；脆弱的

entries.definition: weak and not convincing
entries.definitionCN: 无力的；站不住脚的

normalIntro.en: Flimsy names thinness first, then the weakness of anything built or argued with too little substance.
normalIntro.cn: flimsy 先指「薄」，再指任何用料不足或论证不足之物的脆弱。

normal.en: Flimsy may be linked to flim-flam, the old word for trickery, which also suggests something without substance.
normal.cn: flimsy 可能与表示「欺骗」的古词 flim-flam 有关，那个词同样带有「没有实质」的意味。

normal.en: A flimsy excuse is as thin as paper.
normal.cn: 「a flimsy excuse」就像纸一样薄。

normal.en: Flimsy paper tears before it can carry any weight.
normal.cn: 薄纸还没承载重量就先破了。

normal.en: The comparative is flimsier and the superlative is flimsiest.
normal.cn: 比较级是 flimsier，最高级是 flimsiest。

normal.en: Flimsiness names the quality, and flimsily describes the weak way something is done.
normal.cn: flimsiness 指「薄」的性质，flimsily 描述做得单薄的方式。

abstract.en: Picture tracing paper that rips at a touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一张一碰就裂的描图纸。

abstract.en: See a stick hut shake in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一间树枝小屋在风里摇晃。

abstract.en: Hear an excuse tear apart under one question.
abstract.cn: 想象一个借口被一个问题就撕得粉碎。

examples.en: The flimsy chair broke when he sat on it.
examples.cn: 他刚一坐上去，那把单薄的椅子就坏了。

examples.en: She gave a flimsy reason for missing the class.
examples.cn: 她为缺课给了一个站不住脚的理由。

examples.en: The tent was flimsier than they had expected.
examples.cn: 帐篷比他们预想的还要单薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗林姆齐」——薄得像纸，一碰就散；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: flimsy 来源不确定：十八世纪中期出现，先指织物或纸张又薄又轻，一般认为与十六世纪 flim-flam（胡扯、欺骗）有关，也可能受 film（薄膜）影响；由「薄」引申为「结构脆弱」与「理由站不住脚」。

sensesIntro.en: Flimsy moves from thin material that breaks, to weak construction, and then to excuses and evidence that cannot hold.
sensesIntro.cn: flimsy 从容易破的薄材料，走到不牢固的结构，再走到撑不住的借口与证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of thin paper that tears at a touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张一碰就破的薄纸。

branches.en: Thin material that breaks at once is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 一碰就破的薄材料是最字面的义项。

branches.en: Thin material also explains a weakly built frame.
branches.cn: 薄材料也解释了为什么结构会不牢固。

branches.en: An excuse as thin as paper fails at the first question.
branches.cn: 像纸一样薄的借口经不起第一个追问。

branches.en: Evidence too thin to support a claim is the evidential branch.
branches.cn: 薄到撑不起结论的证据，是这一意象在证据层面的分支。

branches.en: Both a thin box and a thin curtain share lightness and lack of solidity.
branches.cn: 薄箱子和薄窗帘都同样轻飘、不实在。

intro.en: Flimsy is an adjective with the adverb flimsily and the noun flimsiness, but its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: flimsy 是形容词，派生副词 flimsily 与名词 flimsiness，但更早的词源并不确定。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is recorded, so the word is treated as an uncertain English formation and no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 没有记录到拉丁语同源词，因此把该词视为来源不确定的英语构形，不列出拉丁词条。

items.example: The flimsy lid bent at once.
items.exampleCN: 那个单薄的盖子立刻就弯了。

items.example: This box is flimsier than that one.
items.exampleCN: 这个箱子比那个更单薄。

items.example: The flimsiest part is the handle.
items.exampleCN: 最单薄的部分是把手。

items.meaning: in a weak or thin way
items.example: The shelf was flimsily attached.
items.exampleCN: 架子装得很不牢靠。

items.example: The flimsiness of the roof worried them.
items.exampleCN: 屋顶的单薄让他们担心。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms flimsily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 flimsily。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示性质的名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms flimsiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 flimsiness。

items.example: Flim-flam is an older word that may be related.
items.exampleCN: flim-flam 是一个可能相关的更古老的词。

definition_zh: 燧石；打火石；坚硬如石的东西
definition_en: a hard grey stone that can produce sparks when struck
core_image: 两块石头一碰，迸出几点火星
scene: 露营的夜晚没有火柴，他只能靠一块石头生火。He struck the flint until a spark caught the dry grass.
sceneCN: 这里「flint」是「打火石」（第 2 个义项：与钢片相击生火的燧石）；句意：他不断敲击打火石，直到火星点燃干草。

pos.zh: 燧石；打火石；坚硬的东西

derivatives.zh: 由 flint 加 -y 构成，指「燧石的；坚硬冷峻的」
flint 与 lock 构成的复合词，指「燧发枪」
由 flinty 加 -ness 构成，指「坚硬；冷峻」

senses.title: The hard grey stone
senses.definition: a very hard grey stone that breaks into sharp edges
senses.definitionCN: 一种极硬、会裂出锋利边缘的灰色石头
senses.example: The cave floor was covered with pieces of flint.
senses.exampleCN: 洞底散落着许多燧石碎块。
senses.why: The core image is the stone itself, the hard material that makes sparks when struck.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是这块石头本身：一受撞击便迸出火星的坚硬材料，所以第一义直接指燧石。

senses.title: The fire-making stone
senses.definition: a piece of this stone used with steel to light a fire
senses.definitionCN: 与钢片配合用来点火的燧石小块
senses.example: He struck the flint against the steel.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿燧石去击打钢片。
senses.why: The same stone gains a function when paired with steel, so the material becomes a tool for fire.
senses.whyCN: 同一块石头与钢片配合后有了用途，材料便转化为点火的工具，于是产生「打火石」义。

senses.title: A heart as hard as stone
senses.definition: a heart or character that shows no pity or warmth
senses.definitionCN: 毫无怜悯与温情的内心或性格
senses.example: The old man had a heart of flint.
senses.exampleCN: 那个老人有一副铁石心肠。
senses.why: The hardness of the stone becomes a picture of a character that will not soften, which is the figurative branch.
senses.whyCN: 石头的坚硬被用来比喻不肯软化的性格，这就是从实物长出的比喻义。

senses.title: A shaped tool stone
senses.definition: a piece of flint shaped into a tool, blade, or arrowhead
senses.definitionCN: 被加工成工具、刀片或箭头的燧石
senses.example: The museum displays a flint arrowhead.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出一枚燧石箭头。
senses.why: Flint breaks with sharp edges, so early people shaped it into tools and weapons.
senses.whyCN: 燧石裂开后边缘锋利，早期人类便把它打制成工具与武器，于是有了「石器」义。

senses.title: The sparking stone in a lighter
senses.definition: a small piece of material in a lighter that produces a spark
senses.definitionCN: 打火机里产生火星的小块材料
senses.example: The lighter needs a new flint.
senses.exampleCN: 这个打火机需要换一颗新火石。
senses.why: The modern lighter keeps the old fire-making stone in miniature, so the word follows the tool into a new machine.
senses.whyCN: 现代打火机把古老的取火石缩成了小零件，词便随工具进入新机器，形成这一现代义。

intro.en: Flint is an old Germanic word, recorded in English from the earliest period.
intro.cn: flint 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，英语中很早就已出现。

items.en: The reconstructed form flintaz is the common ancestor of the Germanic words for flint.
items.cn: 重构形式 flintaz 是各日耳曼语中「燧石」一词的共同祖先。

items.en: Flint names the stone in Old English texts.
items.cn: 古英语文献中 flint 已经指这种石头。

items.en: Flint and flint stone name the stone and its use in fire making.
items.cn: 中古英语用 flint 与「flint stone」指这种石头及其取火用途。

items.en: Flintlock names a gun whose firing mechanism strikes a flint.
items.cn: flintlock 指用燧石点火的枪，因击发机构敲击燧石而得名。

items.en: Flinty extends the stone to hardness of heart, and the lighter keeps a small flint.
items.cn: flinty 把石头延伸到铁石心肠，打火机里也保留着一颗小火石。

note.en: Flint is a stone word, close to chert and quartz, with flinty and flintlock as its English family.
note.cn: flint 是表示石头的词，与 chert、quartz 同类，英语词族中有 flinty 与 flintlock。

entries.definition: hard and cold like flint
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬冷峻的；燧石般的

entries.definition: an old gun fired by a flint mechanism
entries.definitionCN: 燧发枪

entries.definition: flint used as building stone
entries.definitionCN: 用作建筑石料的燧石

entries.definition: a hard sedimentary rock resembling flint
entries.definitionCN: 燧石岩；一种类似燧石的坚硬沉积岩

entries.definition: a hard mineral found in many rocks
entries.definitionCN: 石英

entries.definition: a very hard grey rock used for building
entries.definitionCN: 花岗岩

normalIntro.en: Flint is an Old English stone word whose Germanic relatives include a gun named after the sparking stone.
normalIntro.cn: flint 是古英语的石头词，其日耳曼语同族词中还有以这种取火石命名的枪。

normal.en: Flint is an Old English word, and German Flinte, a gun, is named for the sparking stone.
normal.cn: flint 是古英语词，德语 Flinte（枪）正是因这种取火石而得名。

normal.en: A heart of flint is a heart as hard as stone.
normal.cn: 「a heart of flint」就是像石头一样硬的心。

normal.en: Flint and steel are the classic pair for striking a spark.
normal.cn: 「flint and steel」是敲出火星的经典组合。

normal.en: Flintlock joins flint with lock, the firing mechanism of an old gun.
normal.cn: flintlock 把 flint 与 lock（旧枪的击发机构）组合在一起。

normal.en: The adjective flinty keeps the idea of hardness and coldness.
normal.cn: 形容词 flinty 保留了「坚硬、冷峻」的意味。

abstract.en: Two stones struck together in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中两块石头猛地相击。

abstract.en: A shower of sparks falling on dry grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一串火星落进干草。

abstract.en: A grey stone heart that will not melt.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗灰色石心，怎么也化不开。

examples.en: The path was laid with broken flints.
examples.cn: 小路是用碎燧石铺成的。

examples.en: A flint arrowhead lay in the soil.
examples.cn: 土里埋着一枚燧石箭头。

examples.en: The lighter refused to spark until he changed the flint.
examples.cn: 打火机一直打不着火，直到他换了火石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗林特」——两块石头一碰就冒火星；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: flint 来自古英语 flint（燧石），可追溯到原始日耳曼语重构形式 flintaz；同族词包括中古荷兰语 vlint 与德语 Flinte（枪，因用燧石点火得名）。更早的来源不确定，一般认为与「坚硬、劈开」的语义有关。

sensesIntro.en: Flint begins as a hard stone, then becomes the fire-making stone, a hard heart, a tool material, and the small stone in a lighter.
sensesIntro.cn: flint 从坚硬的石头出发，依次成为取火石、铁石心肠、石器材料，以及打火机里的小火石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey stone that throws sparks when struck.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块受击便迸出火星的灰色石头。

branches.en: The stone itself is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 石头本身是最字面的义项。

branches.en: Paired with steel, the stone becomes a fire-making tool.
branches.cn: 与钢片配合后，石头成为取火工具。

branches.en: The hardness of stone pictures a heart without pity.
branches.cn: 石头的坚硬被用来比喻没有怜悯的心。

branches.en: Sharp edges made flint a material for tools and weapons.
branches.cn: 锋利的边缘使燧石成为工具与武器的材料。

branches.en: The lighter keeps a small flint for the same spark.
branches.cn: 打火机保留一颗小火石，为的仍是同一个火星。

intro.en: Flint is a Germanic stone noun with the adjective flinty, the noun flintiness, and the compound flintlock.
intro.cn: flint 是日耳曼语系的石头名词，派生形容词 flinty、名词 flintiness，并有复合词 flintlock。

latinIntro.en: Latin used silex for flint, but that word is not a cognate of this Germanic term, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 silex 表示燧石，但它并非这个日耳曼语词的同源词，因此不列出拉丁词条。

items.example: Flint breaks into sharp edges.
items.exampleCN: 燧石会裂出锋利的边缘。

items.example: The field was full of flints.
items.exampleCN: 地里到处都是燧石。

items.example: His flinty stare frightened them.
items.exampleCN: 他冷峻的凝视吓到了他们。

items.example: The flintiness in her voice surprised me.
items.exampleCN: 她声音里的冷峻让我吃惊。

items.meaning: an old gun fired by a flint
items.example: A flintlock hung above the fireplace.
items.exampleCN: 壁炉上方挂着一支燧发枪。

items.example: The wall was built of flintstone.
items.exampleCN: 这面墙是用燧石砌成的。

items.example: The suffix -y forms flinty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 flinty。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示性质的名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms flintiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 flintiness。

items.example: In flintlock, lock names the firing mechanism.
items.exampleCN: 在 flintlock 中，lock 指击发机构。

definition_zh: 翻转；轻抛；快速翻动；轻拍
definition_en: to turn something over quickly, or to move it with a short light motion
core_image: 一枚硬币在空中翻个身，又落回手心
scene: 煎饼在锅里边缘发焦，他手腕一抖就把它翻了过来。He flipped the pancake and caught it neatly in the pan.
sceneCN: 这里「flipped」是「快速翻转」（第 1 个义项：把东西迅速翻个面）；句意：他把煎饼翻了个面，又稳稳地接回锅里。

pos.zh: 翻转；轻抛；快速翻动；轻拍

derivatives.zh: 由 flip 加 -er 构成，指「鳍；脚蹼」
flip 重叠构成的复合词，指「人字拖」，也指「立场反复」
flip 与 book 构成的复合词，指「手翻动画书」

senses.title: To turn over quickly
senses.definition: to turn something over with a quick movement
senses.definitionCN: 用迅速的动作把某物翻个面
senses.example: She flipped the pancake in the pan.
senses.exampleCN: 她把锅里的煎饼翻了个面。
senses.why: The core image is an object turning over in one quick motion, so the first sense is the plain physical turn.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个东西在瞬间翻了个面，所以第一义就是最直接的物理翻转。

senses.title: To toss lightly
senses.definition: to throw something with a light quick movement so that it turns
senses.definitionCN: 用轻快动作把东西抛起，使其翻转
senses.example: He flipped the coin into the air.
senses.exampleCN: 他把硬币抛向空中。
senses.why: A quick turn released into the air becomes a toss, keeping the same spinning motion.
senses.whyCN: 把「快速翻转」释放到空中就成了抛掷，旋转的动作仍是同一个。

senses.title: To turn pages quickly
senses.definition: to turn pages quickly or move through them
senses.definitionCN: 迅速翻动书页，或快速浏览其中内容
senses.example: She flipped through the magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 她快速翻阅那本杂志。
senses.why: Each page turns over like a small flip, so reading quickly borrows the motion of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 每一页都像一次小翻转，因此「快速阅读」借用了手翻页的动作。

senses.title: To lose control of the feelings
senses.definition: to lose control of the emotions, often suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然失去对情绪的控制
senses.example: He flipped when he saw the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 他看到损毁情况时情绪失控了。
senses.why: The mind turns over as suddenly as a flipped switch, which is the emotional branch of the image.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像被按下的开关一样骤然翻转，这就是核心意象在心理层面的分支。

senses.title: A light blow
senses.definition: a quick light hit or movement with the fingers or hand
senses.definitionCN: 用手指或手做出的快速轻拍
senses.example: She gave the switch a flip of her finger.
senses.exampleCN: 她用指尖轻弹了一下开关。
senses.why: The earliest sense is a light strike like a fillip, and the short sharp motion survives in the noun.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意义类似用指尖轻弹，这种短促有力的动作保留在名词义里。

intro.en: Flip appears in English in the seventeenth century, and its source is not settled.
intro.cn: flip 在十七世纪进入英语，来源没有定论。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the seventeenth century with no agreed source.
items.cn: 这个动词最早见于十七世纪，来源没有公认结论。

items.en: Fillip, a light strike with the fingertip, is a likely relative in both sound and sense.
items.cn: fillip（用指尖轻弹）在读音和意义上都可能是近亲。

items.en: Flip records the sense of tossing something with a jerk.
items.cn: flip 记下了「猛地一抛」的意义。

items.en: The word extends to turning pages and to turning the body in the air.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到翻书页，以及身体在空中翻转。

items.en: Flip out and flip side add emotional and figurative uses.
items.cn: 「flip out」与「flip side」增加了情绪化和比喻性的用法。

note.en: Flip is a quick-turn word, with flipper and flip-flop in its family and toss and flick as near neighbours.
note.cn: flip 是表示「快速翻转」的词，词族中有 flipper 与 flip-flop，近邻有 toss 与 flick。

entries.definition: a limb or fin used for swimming
entries.definitionCN: 鳍；脚蹼

entries.definition: a thonged sandal, or a reversal of position
entries.definitionCN: 人字拖；立场反复

entries.definition: a book of pictures that seem to move when flipped
entries.definitionCN: 手翻动画书

entries.definition: to throw something lightly
entries.definitionCN: 轻抛；掷

entries.definition: to hit or move with a quick light movement
entries.definitionCN: 轻弹；轻拂

entries.definition: to turn something over so that the other side faces up
entries.definitionCN: 翻倒；翻转

normalIntro.en: Flip echoes a short light movement, and its family repeats the same quick turn in many shapes.
normalIntro.cn: flip 模仿一种短促轻快的动作，它的词族以多种形态重复着同一个「快速翻转」。

normal.en: Flip is probably echoic or from fillip, the old word for a light fingertip strike.
normal.cn: flip 很可能是拟声词，或来自表示指尖轻弹的古词 fillip。

normal.en: Flip a coin and the coin turns in the air.
normal.cn: 「flip a coin」，硬币就在空中翻转。

normal.en: Flip through a book and the pages turn quickly under your thumb.
normal.cn: 「flip through a book」，书页就在拇指下快速翻过。

normal.en: Flip out means to lose control, as if a switch inside has been flipped.
normal.cn: 「flip out」指失控，就像体内的开关被猛地按下。

normal.en: The compound flip-flop repeats flip and names a sandal that flips as you walk.
normal.cn: 复合词 flip-flop 重复 flip，指走路时会拍打翻转的人字拖。

abstract.en: A pancake rising and turning in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象煎饼腾空而起，翻了个面。

abstract.en: A coin spinning above a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币在桌面上方旋转。

abstract.en: A book whose pages turn in a blur.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书的书页飞快翻过，模糊成一片。

examples.en: He flipped the coin and caught it on his wrist.
examples.cn: 他把硬币抛起，又用手腕接住。

examples.en: She flipped through the pages looking for the map.
examples.cn: 她快速翻页，寻找那张地图。

examples.en: The flip side of the plan is the extra cost.
examples.cn: 这个计划的另一面是额外的成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗利普」——手腕一抖，东西就翻个面；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: flip 来源不确定：十七世纪出现，表「猛地一抛、轻弹」，一般认为与 fillip（用指尖轻弹）有关，也可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语（如挪威语 flippen）；核心义「轻而快地翻过去」。

sensesIntro.en: Flip starts with a quick turn, then a toss in the air, then pages, then a sudden emotional turn, and finally a light blow.
sensesIntro.cn: flip 从快速翻转出发，依次延伸到空中轻抛、翻书页、情绪骤变，最后是轻拍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin turning over in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币在空中翻了个身。

branches.en: A quick physical turn is the central sense.
branches.cn: 快速的物理翻转是中心义项。

branches.en: The turn released into the air becomes a toss.
branches.cn: 把翻转释放到空中，就成为抛掷。

branches.en: Pages turn like small flips under the hand.
branches.cn: 书页在手下像一次次小翻转。

branches.en: A sudden mood change is a turn of the mind.
branches.cn: 情绪骤变是内心的一次翻转。

branches.en: A light blow and a quick turn both use one short sharp movement.
branches.cn: 轻拍与快速翻转都依赖同一种短促有力的动作。

intro.en: Flip is a short English verb and noun with forms in -s, -ed, and -ing, and a family of compounds such as flip-flop and flipbook.
intro.cn: flip 是简短的英语动词兼名词，有 -s、-ed、-ing 等词形，并有 flip-flop、flipbook 等复合词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is known, so the word is treated as echoic or of uncertain northern origin and no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语同源词，因此把该词视为拟声或来源不明的北方词，不列出拉丁词条。

items.example: Flip the fish before it burns.
items.exampleCN: 在鱼烧焦前把它翻个面。

items.meaning: a quick turn or light blow
items.example: The flip of the coin decided the match.
items.exampleCN: 抛硬币决定了这场比赛。

items.meaningCN: 动词第三人称单数形式
items.example: He flips the switch every morning.
items.exampleCN: 他每天早上都会按下开关。

items.example: The car flipped onto its side.
items.exampleCN: 汽车翻倒在路旁。

items.example: The flipping of the pages woke the cat.
items.exampleCN: 翻页的声音吵醒了猫。

items.meaning: a fin or paddle used for swimming
items.example: The seal beat the water with its flippers.
items.exampleCN: 海豹用鳍拍打水面。

items.meaning: a thonged sandal or a reversal
items.example: One flip-flop came off in the mud.
items.exampleCN: 一只人字拖陷在泥里掉了。

items.meaning: a book of pictures that appear to move
items.example: The child made a flipbook of a running horse.
items.exampleCN: 孩子做了一本奔马的手翻动画书。

items.example: The suffix -er forms flipper.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 flipper。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词与动名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms flipping.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 flipping。
